# How to Use AI to Get More TikTok Views (Even With a Small Account)

> **In short:** Small TikTok accounts grow faster by using AI to fix specific weak spots — bad hooks, slow edits, missing captions — instead of chasing viral moments. Find where viewers drop off, and the algorithm will show your video to more people.

A creator with 800 followers can outperform a creator with 80,000 on any given week, and the difference almost never comes down to luck. It comes down to whether viewers stay past the first three seconds — and AI can help you fix that faster than you can on your own.

## Before you start

You'll need:

- A TikTok account (free)
- The TikTok app on your phone
- At least one general AI assistant — ChatGPT, Claude, or Gemini all have free tiers
- About 20 to 30 minutes for your first attempt

You don't need a fancy camera, a ring light, or editing experience. Phone footage in decent light is enough.

## Step 1 — Write a hook in 60 seconds with AI

The first two seconds decide whether someone watches or scrolls past. That opening line is called the **hook**, and it's the single biggest lever you have.

Open your AI assistant and paste this prompt:

> 💬 *"Give me 10 hook ideas for a TikTok about [your topic]. Each hook must be under 12 words, sound natural when spoken out loud, and make the viewer curious enough to keep watching."*

Read the results out loud. If you stumble, the hook is too clever — pick a simpler one. Record three takes and use the one that sounds like something you'd actually say to a friend.

**You'll know it worked when** you can read the hook without pausing and it makes you want to hear the next sentence.

## Step 2 — Script the rest with a simple structure

Most viewers who leave a video do so because they get lost. A clear structure keeps them with you.

Use this prompt:

> 💬 *"Here's my hook: [paste your hook]. Now write a 30-second TikTok script. Use this structure: hook → problem → 2 quick tips → one-line recap. Keep sentences short and easy to say."*

Read the script aloud once. If any sentence takes more than one breath to say, shorten it. Speaking fast isn't the goal — being easy to follow is.

**You'll know it worked when** you can deliver the whole script in 25 to 35 seconds without rushing.

## Step 3 — Edit faster with AI trimming

Raw footage is full of pauses, "um"s, and dead air. Manual trimming takes an hour. AI trimming takes a minute.

Apps like **CapCut** (free, made by the same company that owns TikTok), **Descript**, and **Opus Clip** can analyze your footage, cut out silences, remove filler words, and suggest jump cuts. CapCut's auto-reframe also keeps your face centered when you post in vertical format.

Upload your clip, tap the AI trimming tool, and let it do a first pass. Then watch the result and undo any cuts that feel rushed — AI doesn't know your personality yet.

**You'll know it worked when** your raw 4-minute clip is now a tight 45 to 90 seconds and still feels like you.

## Step 4 — Add captions automatically

Many viewers watch TikTok with the sound off at some point. No captions means no message.

Use the **Captions app**, **CapCut's auto-captions**, or TikTok's built-in caption tool. Each generates text on screen from your audio in seconds.

Always read the captions once before posting. AI usually gets the words right, but it often misses the ones that matter most — names, brand names, and anything in a strong accent. Fix those by hand — it takes 30 seconds and makes a big difference.

**You'll know it worked when** every word on screen matches what you said, including the words you'd think it would obviously get right.

## Step 5 — Make B-roll and visuals with image generators

**B-roll** is the extra footage cut over your voice to keep the picture interesting — and it's what separates a beginner video from one that looks intentional. You don't need to film it.

Use **Midjourney**, **DALL-E**, or the free **Microsoft Designer** image generator to create still images that match what you're saying. Then drop them into CapCut as a 2 to 3 second clip each.

Prompt example:

> 💬 *"A messy kitchen counter with fresh vegetables and a cutting board, soft morning light, photo-realistic."*

Six to eight such images, dropped over a 60-second script, look more polished than shaky phone footage and take about 10 minutes to make.

**You'll know it worked when** your viewer sees a new visual every few seconds and never has time to get bored.

## Step 6 — Read your TikTok analytics to find the drop-off

This is the step almost everyone skips, and it's the one that actually moves the needle.

After a video has been up for 48 hours, open your profile in TikTok and look for **Analytics** under the menu or Creator Tools section. Tap **Content**, choose a video, and check the **average watch time** and the **"watched full video"** percentage.

If you can't see Analytics in your menu, that's normal — TikTok only shows it on Business and Creator accounts, and switching is free. Tap the three-line menu in the top corner, choose **Settings and privacy**, then **Manage account**, and select **Switch to Business account**. Once that flips on, the Analytics tab appears under Creator Tools within a few minutes.

If your average watch time is short but views are decent, your hook is fine but the middle is losing people. If average watch time is high but views are low, the algorithm doesn't know who to show your video to — try a clearer caption and more relevant hashtags.

Use this prompt to plan the fix:

> 💬 *"My TikTok got [X] views but the average watch time was only [Y] seconds out of [Z] total. What are the three most likely reasons people are leaving, and what should I change next time?"*

**You'll know it worked when** you can name one specific thing to change in your next video based on real numbers, not a feeling.

## Common mistakes

- **Using AI captions but skipping the proofread.** AI usually gets the words right, but it often misses the ones that matter most — names, brand names, words in strong accents. Always read once.
- **Letting the AI rewrite your personality.** Your script should sound like you on your most focused day. If it sounds like a press release, simplify it.
- **Posting and forgetting.** The growth happens when you look at analytics and adjust. Posting alone is just noise.
- **Skipping the hook to get to "the good part."** There is no good part if no one stays past the hook. The hook IS the part.
- **Copying trending audios without a plan.** Trends help, but only if they fit your topic. A forced trend confuses both viewers and the algorithm.

## What this means for you

- **If you're just starting out:** Pick one AI tool and one step. Don't try all six at once. The fastest win is almost always Step 1 — a stronger hook.
- **If you've been posting for a few months:** Your bottleneck is probably analytics. Step 6 will tell you exactly where to focus.
- **If you want to grow into a side income:** Focus on average watch time and rewatches, not just view counts. Brands pay for engagement — likes, comments, shares, and saves on a single video — more than for follower numbers. A small account with high engagement often earns more than a big account with bored viewers.
- **If you're nervous about AI making your content feel fake:** Use AI for the boring parts (trimming, captions, B-roll) and keep your own voice for the parts that need to sound human — the hook and the script.

## Wrap-up

Small TikTok accounts don't grow by accident. They grow because the creator learned where viewers drop off, fixed it, and tried again. AI is just a faster way to find and fix those weak spots — the camera, the idea, and the voice still have to be yours. Pick one step from this guide and try it on your next video. You don't need more followers to start; you need one better video than the one before.
